metaDescription: Five angle grinders under $100 compared on disc size, brushless motors, battery capacity and why a corded 4-1/2 inch model still beats most cheap cordless ones.
expertTake: Under $100 a cordless angle grinder is almost always a 3-inch mini, and the TEENO brushless 3-inch kit is the best overall because it combines a brushless motor, 19,500 rpm, two 2.0 Ah batteries and an adjustable guard. The FULLYEA is the only true 4-1/2 inch cordless here, with three speeds and two 4.0 Ah batteries, and the DEWALT DWE4011 is the corded benchmark for people who need real cutting power. Skip every cordless mini for thick steel or heavy grinding, because the discs are small and the batteries drain in minutes.
introParagraphs: An angle grinder is a small, fast motor turning an abrasive disc, and it is the tool for cutting bolts, smoothing welds, removing rust and sharpening blades. It is also one of the most dangerous hand tools, because a disc spinning at ten thousand rpm or more can shatter or kick if it binds.

Cordless versions add freedom and cost, and at a low price they usually shrink the disc to keep the battery small. This guide explains what a cheap cordless grinder can cut, what safety features matter and why a corded model remains the better value for heavy work. The quick picks are above, and the reviews below match each grinder to a job.

products.name: TEENO 16.8V Brushless Cordless 3-Inch Angle Grinder, 19,500 RPM, Two 2.0Ah
products.description:
The TEENO brushless is the best buy because it does the small-grinder job properly. A brushless motor is more efficient than a brushed one, which matters in a tool that pulls heavy current, and it allows a shorter gear head, so the whole tool is easier to handle in tight spaces. A 3-inch disc spinning at 19,500 rpm reaches a rim speed close to a 4-1/2 inch disc at about 13,000 rpm, so it cuts and grinds in the same range.

Two 2.0 Ah batteries let you swap while one charges, which matters because a cordless grinder drains a pack in a few minutes of continuous grinding. A 90 degree adjustable base guard deflects sparks away from your body, and an LED display shows battery and status. Against the other TEENO, the brushless version has the better motor and the guard.

Because the discs are small, they wear faster than 4-1/2 inch discs, and cutting thick steel is slow. Check that any disc you fit is rated for at least the tool's no-load rpm, and wear a face shield, gloves and eye protection. Do not remove the guard. Wear a full face shield, gloves and hearing protection, and keep sparks away from flammable materials.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a compact, efficient grinder for light cutting and rust removal.
pros: Brushless motor for efficiency and a short gear head
cons: 3-inch discs wear faster than 4-1/2 inch discs
Small batteries drain in minutes of heavy grinding

products.name: FULLYEA 4-1/2-Inch Cordless Angle Grinder, Brushless, 12,000 RPM, 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
The FULLYEA is the only grinder in this guide with the standard 4-1/2 inch disc on a cordless platform. That size matters because 4-1/2 inch discs are the most common size, cheap to buy in every type and thick enough to last through a job. It adds a brushless motor, 12,000 rpm and three speed settings, which is rare in a budget grinder.

Speed settings of 6,000, 9,000 and 12,000 rpm let you drop the speed for polishing, wire brushing and cutting plastic or soft metals, where a full-speed disc melts the material. Two 4.0 Ah batteries are the largest in the group, which makes it the best pick for longer jobs. A bottom switch is a safety-minded design, and the brushless motor helps battery life.

Compared with the TEENO, the FULLYEA is bigger and heavier but more capable on thick material. Compared with the corded DEWALT, it gives freedom but not the same sustained power. Always use a side handle and confirm the disc's rated speed exceeds 12,000 rpm. Swap the battery as soon as the tool slows, since a draining pack cuts poorly and wears the disc.
products.bestFor: Users who need a standard-size cordless grinder with speed control.
cons: Cannot match a corded grinder's sustained power

products.name: TEENO 16.8V Cordless 3-Inch Mini Angle Grinder, 19,500 RPM, 2 x 2000mAh
products.description:
This TEENO is the plain mini: a 16.8V system, a 19,500 rpm motor and two 2,000 mAh batteries in a slim body. It is aimed at yard and patio work such as cutting a rusted bolt on a gate, trimming a bolt on a bench or removing paint from a railing, jobs where a full-size grinder is unwieldy.

Its light weight is the selling point, and it reaches tight spaces around gates and fixtures. Compared with the brushless TEENO, it lacks the stated brushless motor, so expect more heat and shorter run time on the same 2.0 Ah packs. The two batteries let you swap, but cutting more than a few bolts will drain both.

The small disc cuts shallowly, so it is best for thin sheet, bolts, rebar stubs and small welds. Keep several discs handy, since mini discs wear in minutes on steel, and match them to the tool's arbor size. Use eye protection and a face shield, and clamp the work, since a grinder kicks if the work moves. Keep spare discs on hand, since mini discs wear faster than the batteries.
products.bestFor: Light yard and workshop cutting where a small tool reaches tight spots.
pros: Slim, light body reaches tight spaces
Low price for a cordless kit

products.name: novorik 16.8V Cordless Mini Angle Grinder, 28,000 RPM, Two 2000mAh, 5 Discs
products.description:
The novorik is the cheapest cordless grinder here, and it says outright that it uses a brushed motor. A brushed motor is simpler and less costly than a brushless design, but it wears its brushes and runs hotter, which suits an occasional tool and not a daily one. The 28,000 rpm no-load speed is very high, which is only possible with a small disc, and it makes disc choice critical.

A high rpm on a tiny disc is tough on discs, so use only discs rated for that speed and replace them at the first sign of cracking. Five cutting discs come in the kit, which is useful because mini discs wear quickly. Two 2,000 mAh batteries and a rubberized handle round out a basic package.

Compared with the brushless TEENO, the novorik costs less but has a less efficient motor and no listed guard adjustment. It is a reasonable tool for trimming a few bolts and cutting thin metal, and a poor one for sustained use. Do not remove the guard, and treat the 28,000 rpm figure as a reason to check every disc before use. Check that the disc is rated for the tool's rpm before every change.
products.bestFor: Occasional users who need to cut a few bolts or thin metal pieces at the lowest price.
pros: Two batteries and five discs included
Very high speed for small discs
cons: Brushed motor runs hotter and wears brushes

products.name: DEWALT DWE4011 4-1/2-Inch Corded Angle Grinder, 7 Amp, One-Touch Guard
products.description:
The DEWALT DWE4011 is included as a corded benchmark, because for heavy cutting and grinding a corded 4-1/2 inch grinder still beats cheap cordless ones. A 7 amp motor at 12,000 rpm sustains power as long as it is plugged in, where a small battery drains in minutes. It is designed for faster material removal and higher overload capacity.

A one-touch guard adjusts without tools, which encourages users to leave the guard in the right position instead of removing it. A hex wrench replaces the usual spanner wrench for disc changes, a hex key found in most tool boxes. Compared with the FULLYEA, it has no batteries to charge and a name-brand service network, but the cord limits reach.

For a toolbox that has one grinder, this is the one to buy if you cut or grind often. The cordless minis are conveniences for light work, while a corded 4-1/2 inch is the workhorse. Wear eye and face protection, use a side handle and let the disc come to full speed before touching the work. Clamp the work, since a grinder kicks if the work moves.
products.bestFor: Anyone who grinds or cuts steel regularly and does not need a battery.
pros: 7 amp motor sustains power with no battery limit
Standard 4-1/2 inch discs are cheap and common

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 3-inch disc, as on the TEENO and novorik, cuts about 3/4 inch deep and wears quickly, while a 4-1/2 inch disc, as on the FULLYEA and DEWALT, is the standard size. Mini grinders are for light work like cutting bolts and thin sheet. For thick steel, buy 4-1/2 inch. A 3-inch disc at 19,500 rpm has a similar rim speed to a 4-1/2 inch disc at about 13,000 rpm, but it has far less material to wear through.

The TEENO brushless and FULLYEA use brushless motors, while the novorik states a brushed motor. A brushless motor runs cooler and makes better use of a small battery. In a grinder, which pulls heavy current, that efficiency shows in run time. A brushless motor also makes a shorter gear head possible, which is why the TEENO brushless is easier to hold in tight spots.

A grinder is one of the hungriest cordless tools. The FULLYEA's two 4.0 Ah batteries last longest, and the 2.0 Ah or 2,000 mAh packs on the minis last only a few minutes of heavy work. Always carry a spare pack. Test battery life with a real cut, because a pack that lasts ten minutes on thin sheet may last two on thick bolts.

A disc must be rated for at least the tool's no-load rpm. The novorik's 28,000 rpm and the TEENO's 19,500 rpm require small discs rated for those speeds, while the FULLYEA and DEWALT need discs rated above 12,000 rpm. Never use a disc rated below the tool's speed. Always check the disc's printed maximum rpm against the tool, and discard any disc that is cracked or wet.

The TEENO's 90 degree adjustable guard and the DEWALT's one-touch guard deflect sparks and shield you if a disc shatters. A guard that is hard to adjust gets removed. Always use a side handle, a face shield and gloves. Spark deflection matters most when you cut overhead, so adjust the guard before you start.

Cordless grinders are convenient but limited by battery. A corded 4-1/2 inch grinder like the DEWALT sustains power indefinitely and often costs less. Choose cordless only if you work away from outlets or in tight places. If you already own a corded drill or saw, you may be better off buying a corded grinder and saving the battery cost.

specDecoder.meaning: The disc speed with nothing to cut. It falls under load. Rim speed, not rpm, is what matters to the disc, and it depends on both rpm and diameter.
specDecoder.watchFor: The novorik's 28,000 rpm is only safe with discs rated for it.

specDecoder.meaning: The size of the abrasive wheel, which sets cut depth and rim speed. Large batteries add weight, so a 4.0 Ah pack makes the tool front-heavy.
specDecoder.watchFor: A smaller disc spins faster to compensate, so rpm figures are not comparable across sizes.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor with electronic switching and no brushes. Corded grinders list amps, while cordless ones list voltage, so the figures do not compare.
specDecoder.watchFor: The novorik is brushed, and the other TEENO listing does not say brushless.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity. 2,000 mAh equals 2.0 Ah. Unit conversions matter, since 2,000 mAh is the same as 2.0 Ah.
specDecoder.watchFor: Many listings mix the two units.

specDecoder.meaning: Current draw, a proxy for motor power. The DEWALT is 7 amps. A disc rated for 12,000 rpm should not be used on a 19,500 rpm tool.
specDecoder.watchFor: Amps are not comparable with cordless voltage.

maintenance.why: A cracked disc can shatter. Replace it. Remove the battery before changing discs.
A loose guard is dangerous. Wipe metal dust from the vents.
Metal dust clogs vents. Check the guard clamp.
Heat ages lithium cells. Replace worn bearings if the tool is noisy.
A loose handle reduces control. Store discs dry and flat.

faq.q: Can a cordless grinder replace a corded one?
faq.a: For light work, yes. For heavy grinding, corded is better. Let the disc reach full speed before touching the work.
It deflects sparks and shields you if a disc breaks. Never remove it. Clamp the work, and keep the guard between you and the disc.
A disc rated for at least the tool's rpm and sized for its arbor. Never use a disc past its expiry date or with visible damage.
A few minutes of heavy cutting on a 2.0 Ah pack.
For bolts and thin sheet, yes. For thicker material, use 4-1/2 inch.

faq.q: What safety gear should I wear?
faq.a: Eye and face protection, gloves, hearing protection and a dust mask.
